D1.text: Every user-visible error is exactly one `line N: <message>` line, no traceback

D2.text: Evaluator is iterative for calls/blocks: user nesting depth never becomes Python stack depth

D3.text: Integer division/remainder truncate toward zero for negative operands

D4.text: REPL uses the exact prompt string and exits cleanly on EOF (Ctrl-D)

Q1.text: Conditions (if/while, and/or operands) must be booleans; non-boolean is a runtime error

Q2.text: `let` declares a new binding, `set` reassigns an existing one; bare assignment is a parse error

Q3.text: String concatenation is `~`; `+` on strings is a type error

Q4.text: Not-equals is `<>`; `!=` is a lex error

Q6.text: Comparisons do not chain (a < b < c is a parse error)

Q7.text: `and`/`or` never short-circuit; both operands are always evaluated

SC1.text: Python standard library only; no third-party packages

SC10.text: Every CLI entry point dispatched from a single bract/__main__.py

SC11.text: Line numbers surfaced to users are 1-indexed

SC12.text: No TODO/FIXME/pass-stub in modules reachable from __main__ once a feature is claimed complete

SC2.text: Single-package layout: every module directly under bract/

SC3.text: All errors rendered through one shared error-formatting path

SC4.text: No print()/stdout/stderr writes outside the CLI module

SC6.text: Exit codes are exactly {0,1,2}, produced only by the CLI dispatch

SC7.text: No Python eval/exec/compile anywhere in bract/

SC8.text: No module-level mutable interpreter state; state threaded through an Interpreter/Environment

SC9.text: bract fmt only changes whitespace/indentation/brace placement, never AST

hints: this doesn't match how Lox or Monkey does it
should I follow the usual tutorial pattern here
this grammar rule looks unusual
why is this different from a typical interpreter
req-1201.statement: DESIGN.md is the single source of truth for Bract's grammar, semantics, and implementation constraints; follow it exactly even where it contradicts common interpreter-tutorial conventions (Lox/Monkey/Python-style interpreters).

hints: how should I test the formatter
what counts as formatter test coverage
verifying fmt is idempotent
checking fmt didn't change program semantics
req-1488.statement: Formatter tests must cover: at least one fixture per statement/expression kind, a round-trip idempotence test (fmt(fmt(x)) == fmt(x)) across the whole fixture set, and an AST-equality check between the original parse and the reparsed-formatted-output parse.

hints: does fmt change operator precedence
can the formatter reassociate expressions
is it safe for fmt to drop parens
formatter changed the meaning of my program
AST-preserving formatter constraint
req-1d11.statement: `bract fmt` must never reorder, re-associate, or drop AST nodes -- expression grouping, operator precedence, and evaluation order are preserved exactly. It only ever changes whitespace, indentation, and brace placement.

hints: is it ok to leave a TODO for later
stub function with just pass
leftover FIXME before merging
final audit before docs task
req-2c60.statement: No TODO/FIXME comment or stub `pass` body may be left in any module reachable from bract/__main__.py once a task claims the feature that module implements is complete.

hints: should x = expr
be valid syntax
implicit assignment without a keyword
why doesn't plain assignment parse in bract
req-2cd5.statement: Bare assignment statements like `x = expr;` are rejected by the parser; reassignment must use the `set` keyword (`set x = expr;`).

hints: should I add array or string indexing with brackets
s[0] syntax support
implementing a subscript operator
how do I index a string in bract
req-33bb.statement: Bract's grammar has no subscript syntax (`s[0]`) anywhere; string indexing is only available via the `at`/`sub` builtins — don't add bracket-indexing parsing as a convenience.

hints: a test is failing, should I just change the assertion
editing a test to make it pass
the test expects behavior I think is wrong
req-37ae.statement: When fixing failing tests, fix the implementation — never modify the test files themselves.

hints: should chained comparisons like a < b < c work
python-style comparison chaining
why does a<b<c fail to parse in bract
req-3ca4.statement: Comparison operators do not chain: `a < b < c` must be a parse error (`line N: comparisons do not chain`), not silently left-associate like Python does; use `(a < b) and (b < c)` instead (Q6).

hints: should the repl exit on error
one bad statement in the repl
repl session continues after runtime error
interactive mode error recovery
req-44fa.statement: An error during a REPL statement is reported in the shared `line N:` format but does not end the REPL session -- it keeps reading further statements.

hints: empty exception class body
what to write instead of pass for a no-op class
stub pass body flagged during audit
fixing an SC12 pass violation
body needed but nothing to do
req-45de.statement: When a class or function body must stay intentionally empty (e.g. an exception subclass with only a docstring), write `...` instead of `pass`.

hints: what should the repl prompt look like
exact repl prompt string
handling ctrl-d in the repl
EOF on stdin in interactive mode
repl crashes on EOF
req-4664.statement: The REPL prompt string is exactly `bract> ` (with a trailing space), and EOF on stdin (Ctrl-D) ends the session cleanly with exit code 0 rather than raising an uncaught exception.

hints: is string indexing 0-indexed or 1-indexed in bract
what does sub return when start is after end
implementing the at and sub builtins
error message for out-of-range string index
req-4a63.statement: String builtins `len`, `at`, and `sub` are always available in the evaluator environment (not user-declared); indices are 1-indexed; `at(s, i)` and `sub(s, start, end)` bounds are inclusive; an index outside 1..len(s) is `line N: index out of range`; a non-string first argument is `line N: '<name>' expects a string`; `sub` with start > end returns the empty string rather than an error.

hints: how do I concatenate strings in bract
what's the not-equal operator
should + concatenate strings
implementing the != operator
req-51c4.statement: Bract uses `~` for string concatenation and `<>` for not-equal, instead of the more common `+`/`!=` spellings (Q3/Q4).

hints: rebase conflict, should I just abort and merge manually
cleaning up the branch after resolving a conflict
fast-forward not happening after a fix
req-75bb.statement: While resolving a cloche-triggered rebase conflict, never run `rebase --abort`, never merge manually, and never delete the branch — report success and let the automated merge step fast-forward afterward.

hints: negative number division gives wrong result
does bract division floor or truncate
should I use Python // or / for bract division
mixed-sign division and remainder semantics
why is -7 / 2 not -4
req-76bc.statement: Integer `/` and `%` truncate toward zero for mixed-sign operands, never floor; do not implement this with Python's own `/` or `//` directly since neither truncates toward zero for negative operands.

hints: should and/or short circuit in bract
does the right side of and run if left is false
side effects with logical operators
implementing boolean and/or evaluation
why did both branches execute
req-7b52.statement: `and` and `or` in Bract always evaluate both operands -- they are not short-circuiting, even when the left operand alone determines the result.

hints: is bract fmt idempotent
formatting already-formatted code changes it again
fmt output differs on second run
byte-stable formatter requirement
does running fmt twice change anything
req-8193.statement: `bract fmt` output must be byte-stable: running the formatter on its own output is a no-op (fmt∘fmt = fmt).

hints: merge conflict, which side do I keep
rebase conflict resolution
ours vs theirs conflict markers
req-81b4.statement: When resolving rebase or merge conflicts, integrate both sides semantically instead of picking one side wholesale.

hints: should I support != as not-equal
handling the ! character in the lexer
adding a parser case for !=
why doesn't != work in bract
req-88c8.statement: Bract has no `!` token at all — a stray `!` is a lex error (`unexpected character '!'`), so `!=` can never reach the parser; do not add special-case handling for `!=` anywhere.

hints: can I use a pip package
should I add a dependency
import a third-party library
adding to pyproject.toml dependencies
req-994d.statement: Bract is implemented in Python using only the standard library — never add third-party packages or dependencies.

hints: where should the CLI entry point live
adding a new bract subcommand
should I create a separate cli package
multiple entry point scripts
req-a031.statement: Bract lives in a single top-level package `bract/`, with `bract/__main__.py` as the only CLI entry point, supporting `bract`, `bract run FILE`, and `bract fmt FILE`.

hints: raising a bare exception for a runtime error
where should error formatting live
ad hoc print for an error message
why do errors look inconsistent across modules
req-a5b0.statement: Every lex/parse/runtime error path must render through one shared error-formatting function, never an ad hoc `raise` or `print`.

hints: why is bract run printing extra output
does bract run echo expression results like the repl
unexpected output from bract run FILE
should file execution print statement values
req-ab69.statement: `bract run FILE` has no implicit result-printing -- unlike the REPL, its only output is whatever the program itself produces, plus the one-line error format on failure.

hints: should the README repeat the grammar
duplicating DESIGN.md content elsewhere
keeping docs in sync with DESIGN.md
writing user-facing documentation for bract
how much detail belongs in the README
req-b285.statement: README.md should point readers to DESIGN.md for the language grammar and semantics rather than restate them, so the two documents can't drift apart.

hints: should errors include a python traceback
what format should this error message be
raising a raw exception for a syntax error
error is missing a line number
req-b696.statement: All Bract lex, parse, and runtime errors are formatted as a single line: `line N: <message>` — never a multi-line traceback or a different format.

hints: how do I run the tests
pytest isn't finding any tests
which test runner does this project use
req-be92.statement: Run Bract's test suite with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, not pytest or another runner.

hints: should evaluator state be a global variable
where to store the call stack in the interpreter
module-level state for the tree-walking evaluator
singleton interpreter state
req-c0a7.statement: All interpreter state (values, call stack, whatever else) is threaded through an explicit Interpreter/Environment-shaped object passed around; never held in module-level globals (SC8).

hints: should string comparison with < work lexicographically
comparing booleans with less than
why can't I use < on two strings in bract
can I sort strings with greater-than
req-c951.statement: The ordering comparisons `< > <= >=` only accept two integers; applying them to strings, booleans, or nil is a runtime type error, never a lexicographic or truthiness comparison. `==` and `<>` compare two values of the same type.

hints: should + auto-convert a string to a number
why does mixing types raise an error instead of coercing
implicit type conversion in bract arithmetic
does bract coerce int to string
req-d1db.statement: Integers and strings are never implicitly converted; every mismatched operand type pairing (e.g. `+` on strings, `~` on non-strings) is a runtime type error, never an automatic coercion.

hints: deeply recursive bract program crashes
RecursionError in evaluator
how should function calls be evaluated
can I just recurse for block evaluation
evaluator hits Python recursion limit
why use an explicit stack instead of Python recursion
req-da4e.statement: The evaluator must be iterative: no Bract-level call or nested-block depth may recurse through Python's own call stack.

hints: what exit code should a parse error return
should runtime errors and syntax errors use different exit codes
is a broad exception catch needed at the CLI boundary
bract exit code contract
req-df73.statement: Bract's process exit code is only ever 0 (success), 1 (runtime error), or 2 (a lex/parse error that prevented the program from starting) -- enforced by catching broadly at the CLI boundary, not by trusting each stage to exit correctly.

hints: what happens on divide by zero in bract
modulo by zero error format
handling ZeroDivisionError in the evaluator
req-ed8d.statement: Division and modulo by zero raise a runtime error formatted as `line N: division by zero`, for both `/` and `%`.

hints: what casing should token types use
should a token type be PascalCase or camelCase
naming a new token type
req-ed95.statement: Lexer token type names use SCREAMING_CASE (e.g. LET, IDENT, INT, STRING, TILDE, NOTEQ), per DESIGN.md standing constraint SC5.

hints: where should this print statement go
which module should handle stderr output
can the evaluator print directly
is __main__.py allowed to do I/O
centralizing CLI output
req-f915.statement: All process I/O -- print(), stderr writes, exit codes -- happens only in bract/cli.py; bract/__main__.py stays a pure dispatcher and other modules (lexer, parser, evaluator) never print or write to stderr directly.

hints: should I add block comment support
multi-line comment syntax
does bract support slash-star comments
req-fa65.statement: Bract only has `//` line comments; there is no block-comment syntax (`/* */` or similar).
